title: Telecommunications Amendment (Giving the Community Rights on Phone Towers) Bill 2014
short_title: Telecommunications Amendment (Giving the Community Rights on Phone Towers) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would tighten rules for mobile phone towers and associated infrastructure by expanding notification, changing permit criteria and creating rights to review installation approvals.
Carriers would notify landowners and occupiers within 500 metres, with the advance notice period extended from 10 business days to 30 business days.
Facilities near community-sensitive sites would need to be at least 100 metres away, and alternative, less sensitive locations would have to be unfeasible.
changes: Towers could no longer be designated through instruments such as the low-impact facilities determination.
Tower height measurements would include antennae extending above the structure.
Decisions to issue installation permits could be reviewed by the Administrative Appeals Tribunal.
The Australian Communications and Media Authority would have to inform the public about infrastructure rather than having a discretion to do so.
summary.affected: Telecommunications carriers, nearby landowners and occupiers and the Australian Communications and Media Authority are affected.
